name: Dual-band GNSS module with compass, NavIC
summary: An L1 and L5 GNSS receiver with patch antenna and compass in a mast-mounted puck, with NavIC support. Sample data: the supplier and every figure here are fictional.

buyers: Drone makers building for defence and government tenders
demand.reason: GNSS modules are 90 to 95 percent imported in Indian drones, the highest share of any part in the DFI estimate. NavIC support matters to Indian government buyers.

sources.title: Drone Federation India white paper on import dependence, reported by Business Standard, 18 Nov 2026
Army drone procurement and the ban on Chinese parts, Rediff and Business Standard, 23 Nov 2026

checked: Constellations, bands, update rate and mass as stated by the supplier
notChecked: Accuracy or time to first fix, not measured
Whether BeiDou can be switched off for buyers who must exclude it

parts.name: Base housing
parts.role: Hold the board and mount the module to the mast.
parts.whatItDoes: A moulded plastic base with a screw boss for the GPS mast and a slot for the cable.
parts.whyItMatters: The base sets how far the antenna sits from carbon and wiring, which block and distort signals.
buyingChecks: Ask whether the plastic is UV-stabilised
Check the mast fitting matches your frame
Ask for the ingress rating of the closed housing

parts.name: Compass
parts.role: Measure heading from the Earth's magnetic field.
parts.whatItDoes: A three-axis magnetometer on the underside of the board, mounted in the module so it sits far from motor and power wiring.
parts.whyItMatters: Satellite position gives no heading at hover. A compass that reads motor current instead of north sends the drone the wrong way.
buyingChecks: Ask for the magnetometer part number
Ask how far the module must sit from power wiring
Check the board orientation arrow is marked

parts.name: Receiver board
parts.role: Turn satellite signals into position, speed and time.
parts.whatItDoes: The board carries the GNSS receiver chip, its crystal, a low-noise amplifier and a backup supply for fast restarts.
parts.whyItMatters: The receiver chip decides which constellations and bands are tracked. Dual-band L1 and L5 tracking cuts errors from the ionosphere and from reflections.
parts.material: FR-4 board with RF shield can
buyingChecks: Ask for the receiver chip maker and model
Ask which constellations and bands are tracked, including NavIC
Ask for update rate and time to first fix, measured outdoors

parts.name: Patch antenna
parts.role: Receive satellite signals from the sky.
parts.whatItDoes: A square ceramic patch with a silver top layer, tuned to the GNSS bands. It faces up and sits on a ground plane.
parts.whyItMatters: Antenna size and tuning matter more than the receiver for weak-signal tracking. A patch tuned for L1 only cannot use L5.
buyingChecks: Ask which bands the antenna is tuned for
Ask for antenna gain and axial ratio
Check the patch is not covered by metal or carbon in your build

parts.name: Top cover
parts.role: Protect the antenna without blocking signals.
parts.whatItDoes: A domed radio-transparent cover that clips or screws onto the base.
parts.whyItMatters: Paint, metallic finishes or thick walls weaken signals. The cover must stay clear to radio and to sunlight damage.
buyingChecks: Ask whether the cover paint is radio-transparent
Check the seal between cover and base

parts.name: Cable and connector
parts.role: Carry power, serial data and compass data to the flight controller.
parts.whatItDoes: A shielded multi-core cable ending in a locking connector that matches the flight controller's GPS port.
parts.whyItMatters: Cable faults show up as random position jumps. Shielding and locking connectors avoid most of them.
parts.material: Shielded PVC or silicone cable with locking connector
buyingChecks: Check the connector pinout matches your flight controller
Ask whether the cable is shielded
